func_800144E8_150E8.title: Load and decode a resource
func_800144E8_150E8.summary: Loads a resource into scratch memory, decodes PIC image data or copies raw bytes into a caller-provided output buffer, and returns the output end pointer.
func_800144E8_150E8.declaration: extern unsigned char *func_800144E8_150E8(unsigned int resource_id, void *packed_scratch, void *decoded_out);
behavior: Calls func_800145B4_151B4 to load the selected resource into packed_scratch. If the loaded data begins with the ASCII bytes PIC, it parses the picture header and decodes pixels into decoded_out; otherwise it copies the loaded byte range unchanged into decoded_out.

For PIC input, the return advances by the decoded byte count from the parsed metadata. For non-PIC input, it advances by the loaded byte count. The routine writes back the output data cache before returning.

Loading and decoding are synchronous. The resource tables and PI manager must already be initialized, and callers should perform this work at a resource-initialization boundary rather than once per frame.

parameters.name: resource_id
parameters.description: General-file or packed-resource ID accepted by the underlying resource loader.

parameters.name: packed_scratch
parameters.description: Caller-owned, DMA-aligned writable scratch buffer large enough for the loaded representation.

parameters.name: decoded_out
parameters.description: Caller-owned writable destination large enough for the raw copy or decoded picture data.

func_800144E8_150E8.returns: Pointer one byte past the output written to decoded_out. If the loader produces no bytes, returns decoded_out unchanged.
cautions: Neither destination has a capacity argument. Establish both the stored size and the maximum decoded size for the exact resource before calling; checking the returned pointer afterward cannot prevent an overrun.
Use separate, nonoverlapping packed and decoded buffers. The picture decoder resets and mutates resident global workspace, so serialize this function with other picture decodes on the game thread.

The packed destination must satisfy the PI DMA alignment requirements. If decoded bytes will be referenced by native display-list or segmented texture commands, keep them in original 8 MiB RDRAM and retain them for the renderer's full lifetime.
func_800144E8_150E8.exampleExplanation: This example uses a verified resource whose ROM address, stored size, and decoded size are known in advance. Those checks are part of the asset contract.
